newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF eyes strong growth with drugs.
newsitem.headline: BASF eyes strong growth with drugs.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group BASF AG said on Wednesday it plans to post sales of four to five billion marks in its drugs business by the year 2000 focusing largely on innovative new products.
"With the planned launches of new products, we expect to post sales of four to five billion marks annually by the year 2000," BASF chief executive Juergen Strube told journalists.

Strube said the group expects to receive approval to launch six to seven new drugs next year. This will include the group's obesity drug Meridia, which was granted U.S. FDA approval earlier this week.
Meridia, poised to become one of BASF's leading drugs, is expected to show annual sales of around 800 million marks, Strube added.
For 1996 BASF expects to post drug sales of 3.4 billion marks, Strube said.

BASF's health and nutrition business, instrumental to nine month results, posted an 18.4 percent jump in sales to 7.1 bilion marks. It is the group's third largest business area after plastics and fibres and colorants and finishing products.
Last year the health and nutrition business posted sales of nearly eight billion marks.
Strube also stressed that BASF was most interested in strengthening its product palette of ethical drugs, while remaining interested in the lucrative generics drug field.
Generic drugs are products whose patent protection has lapsed.
Strube said that the group's acquisition of U.K. chemist chain Boots drugs business has largely fuelled BASF's rise in drugs sector results.
Strube left open the possibility of making further acquisitions, something analysts said may be quite likely now that the company has largely digested the Boots acquisition.
